subject: ela
intro: Tenth graders analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text (such as a section or chapter). Structure is how the author arranges parts so that each develops and refines the argument.

items.prompt:
An essay's first section defines a problem, and a later section refines it by distinguishing two kinds of the problem.

How does the later section DEVELOP the idea?

steps: The later section adds nuance by distinguishing two types.
So it refines the idea by making the problem more precise.
solution.answer: It refines the idea by distinguishing two kinds of the problem, adding precision.

items.prompt:
A single paragraph gives a vivid example right after a general claim.

How does that paragraph function?

steps: The example illustrates and supports the general claim.
So the paragraph develops the claim with concrete support.
solution.answer: It develops the claim by illustrating it with a concrete example.

items.prompt: Why analyze how SECTIONS develop and refine ideas?

steps: Each part builds on and sharpens the argument.
So it shows how the text's parts work together to make the point.
solution.answer: To see how the parts work together to build and sharpen the point.

items.prompt: How an author arranges parts is the ____.
A paragraph giving an example ____ a claim.
Adding nuance to an idea ____ it.
